slots.title: August PPI up 0.4% month over month
slots.body:
August producer price inflation (wholesale-level prices): **+0.4%** month over month — estimate **0.4%**, prior month **+0.1%**.

Year over year: **5.4%** vs estimate **5.3%** (prior **4.8%**).

Core producer prices excluding food and energy: **+0.2%** MoM vs estimate **0.3%**; core PPI year over year **4.6%**, in line with the estimate.

The report landed the same morning as initial jobless claims at **206K** (estimate **205K**).

Coverage ahead of Friday’s consumer inflation print tied the prior session’s tone to energy and long-term bond yields.

Which PPI line do you watch first — headline, core, or the ex-food-energy-trade measure?

slots.title: Bessent cites Monday bank sanction on Iran
slots.body:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said a **“large bank”** will be sanctioned **Monday**, without naming the institution or country in the remarks cited by Reuters and CNBC.

The comment was framed as part of U.S. economic measures against Iran since the Mideast conflict that began in February.

Oil and risk assets were already in focus after the prior session: Brent crude **107.75** (**+0.1%**); the oil ETF **$USO** **+5.6%** to **158.38** on that close.

The **Nikkei 225** finished **−2.8%**; WSJ tied the move to chip names and concerns about the Iran war and energy costs.

What do you track first when sanctions headlines hit — oil, the dollar, or bank stocks?

slots.title: U.S. session recap — Sept. 10, 2026
slots.body:
U.S. equity indexes closed lower on Sept. 10 ahead of the next morning’s consumer inflation report.
The S&P 500 finished at 7,592.30, down 44.06 points (−0.6%).
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was at 52,064.10 (−0.6%), and the Nasdaq Composite at 26,081.72 (−0.7%).
The Russell 2000 lagged at 2,890.95 (−1.0%).

Producer prices for August printed at 12:30 ET.
Headline PPI rose 0.4% month over month (estimate 0.4%), with PPI up 5.4% year over year.
Core PPI was 0.2% MoM vs 0.3% estimated.
Initial jobless claims for the Sept. 5 week were 206K (estimate 205K).
Existing home sales for August were 3.98M annualized, with sales down 2.0% MoM.

The CBOE Volatility Index rose 8.4% to 17.84.
Treasury levels in the injected snapshot (dated Sept. 8) showed the 10-year at 4.8% and the 30-year at 5.2%, with a 2s10s spread of 0.41.

Oil exposure rallied in the session data: the United States Oil Fund ($USO) closed up 5.6% at 158.38.
Brent crude was little changed at 107.75 (+0.1%).
Gold futures were at 4,365.50 (−0.9%).
The dollar proxy ($UUP) ticked up 0.2% to 28.03.
Bitcoin was at 76,822.25 (+0.4%).

Overseas indexes were soft in the same window: Nikkei 225 −2.8%, Hang Seng −1.1%, FTSE 100 −0.6%.

On Nasdaq sector averages, real estate led declines (−2.1%) and utilities −1.3%.
Consumer cyclical and industrials each averaged about +0.8%; technology averaged +0.2%.

Oracle ($ORCL) reported EPS 1.92 vs 1.74 estimated and revenue about $19.35B vs about $19.13B estimated, and the stock closed −5.2% at 153.17.
Adobe ($ADBE) beat on EPS (6.13 vs 6.08) and revenue (~$6.76B vs ~$6.69B estimated) and still finished −2.4% at 248.83.
Macy’s ($M) posted EPS 0.40 vs 0.37 estimated and revenue $4.87B vs $4.81B estimated; shares closed −4.7% at 20.50.
Copart ($CPRT) reported EPS 0.35 vs 0.38 estimated with revenue above the estimate and closed −4.0% at 30.75.

Among widely followed large caps, $META −1.4% to 644.38, $TSLA −1.2% to 363.56, $UNH −1.2% to 388.28, and $HD −1.5% to 305.69.
$GOOGL and $GOOG each closed about +0.6%.
$MSFT was flat to slightly up at 492.44 (+0.2%).

Semiconductor and equipment names were broadly lower: $INTC −5.6%, $AMD −3.4%, $NVDA −2.4%, $ASML −2.4%, and $TSM −1.7%, on a day the Nasdaq was down 0.7%.
